heading: Identity-slot join required on all multi-pattern rules
text:
### Identity-slot join required on all multi-pattern rules [LNLS.3.3]

A `where` clause in a multi-pattern rule (one that references bindings
from two or more patterns) must contain equality constraints that pin
the **full declared `key` ([LFAC.1.7]) of a `logical`-lifecycle schema
on one side** to that of a **`logical`-lifecycle schema on the other
side** — one equality per `key` slot when the key is composite.
Any other form of cross-pattern equality or inequality is a compile error.

Formally: the required constraint is a conjunction of equalities, one per
`key` slot:

$\bigwedge_{i} \; A.k_i = B.k_i$

where:
- $A$ and $B$ are bindings from distinct patterns,
- the schema of $A$ uses `logical` lifecycle and $A.k_i$ ranges over
  its declared `key` slots,
- the schema of $B$ uses `logical` lifecycle and $B.k_i$ ranges over
  its declared `key` slots,
- the anchor pins each side's complete key, so each side resolves to at
  most one live fact.

**A singleton is pinned by construction.** A `logical` schema whose key is
empty holds at most one live fact ([LFAC.1.7.2]), so its side of a join resolves
to at most one fact with no equality at all. Between a singleton and a keyed
`logical` schema, the anchor pins the keyed schema's full key, each key slot
equal to a slot of the singleton, and each such slot of the singleton must be
declared non-nullable: it stands in for a key slot, and a key slot is never
null ([LNUL.8.10]). The compiler refuses an anchor on a nullable singleton slot
with `DS_VALIDATE_NOLINSCAN_JOIN_ANCHOR_C`. Between two singletons, no equality
is required.

**Every pattern after the first is anchored to an earlier one, positive or
negated.** In pattern-declaration order, each pattern after the first must be
pinned this way to a pattern declared before it. A negated pattern whose
`where` references no earlier binding is exempt: it asks only whether a matching
fact exists, and when that answer changes, every token it blocks or releases is
part of the result, not a scan. One anchored pair is not
enough in a rule of three or more patterns: a pattern anchored to nothing
before it joins by scan, and [LNLS.5.1]'s right-activation half — a new fact
probing for exactly one candidate token — needs a complete key on the side the
fact arrives at.

Additional constraints (range comparisons, further equality tests
between other slots) are allowed on top of this anchor.
Single-pattern `where` clauses (alpha tests) are unrestricted.

**Why this is the complete no-linear-scan condition**: the index
(lmem_idx / ralpha_idx) gives O(matched) where matched
is the number of facts sharing the join-key value.  An EQ anchor alone
only guarantees an index exists — it does not guarantee O(1).
An EQ anchor on the full declared `key` of a `logical` schema
guarantees O(1) because `logical` retract-and-replace semantics ensure
**at most one live fact per key-tuple**.  J_max = 1 is enforced by the
schema lifecycle, not by the programmer's discipline.

Joining on a non-`key` slot, or on only part of a composite key, even
of a `logical` schema, can produce J_max > 1 (multiple facts sharing
the matched value) and is therefore excluded.  Joining on any slot of a `ttl`-lifecycle
schema is excluded because `ttl` facts accumulate — multiple events
per key is the normal case.

The idiomatic `linear_scan: false` pattern for "join entity state with the
latest event" is a `logical` projection maintained by a separate rule.

The refusals and their codes are [LNLS.3.3a], [LNLS.3.3b] and [LNLS.3.3c].

idris.name: Lnul_8_10__same_typed
idris.note: Two non-null values of one type: what a `linear_scan: false` anchor compares, since it pins `key` slots ([LNLS.3.3]) and a `key` slot is never null ([LNUL.8.10]).

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__typed_anchor_decided
idris.note: A NOLINSCAN ANCHOR IS DECIDED: an equality of two non-null values of one type answers true or false, never null and never a trap, so `iret_7_5_1__probe_negated`'s condition holds for every `no` node a `linear_scan: false` program can load.

idris.name: lnls_3_3__negated_anchor_probe
idris.note: A no node probes on its anchor without loss when both anchored slots are non-null and of one type on every candidate. The keyed form gives that premise ([LNUL.8.10]). The singleton form gives it through [LNLS.3.3]'s refusal of an anchor on a nullable singleton slot, which the model does not state, so there the theorem assumes what the clause guarantees.

idris.name: Lnls_3_3__anchor
idris.note: A FULL-KEY ANCHOR on the right pattern: the join test implies that the candidate is of an entity-lifecycle kind and carries the key the prefix pins; further constraints on top are allowed, as the clause allows them -- the test may be stronger, never weaker.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1
idris.note: J_max = 1 is enforced by the lifecycle, as the clause says: two candidates joining one token under the anchor are one fact.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_after_history
idris.note: THEOREM 5, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network, at every node whose join test is a full-key anchor on an entity-lifecycle kind, every token joins at most one fact of the node's memory. The clause's left-activation half. Its right-activation half -- exactly one left-memory token per key -- needs every pattern of the prefix anchored, not only the right one: with a pattern of the prefix unconstrained by the anchor, tokens differing in that pattern share the key.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_engine
idris.note: At any engine with the view, an anchored node offers each token at most one candidate.
